message.reasoning:
I'm mapping out the full set of methods and branches in DefaultKeyedValues2D that need JUnit 4 coverage, including constructors, getters, key/index lookups with null and sorting variations, and value accessors by row/column key.

I'm working through the mutation methods too—addValue, setValue, removeValue, removeRow, removeColumn, clear—plus equals, hashCode, and clone, noting the conditional logic each contains.

For getValue(int, int), I'm considering whether the null-check on rowData is actually reachable, since the rows list only ever gets populated with real DefaultKeyedValues instances through setValue, so that branch may be practically unreachable in normal usage.

I'm now sketching out concrete test cases: for setValue/addValue I want to cover adding a new row/column, updating existing values, and triggering the sorted insertion path with sortRowKeys enabled. For getValue(int,int) I need normal retrieval, a case where the column exists structurally but not in that row, and out-of-bounds indices. For getValue(Comparable,Comparable) I'm listing null-key checks, unknown-key exceptions for both row and column, and the case where the value simply hasn't been set. And for getRowIndex I'm covering the null-key check and both the sorted and unsorted lookup paths.

I'm also planning tests for getColumnIndex, and for removeValue where removing the last value in a row or column should cause that row/column to be removed entirely versus cases where other values remain. For removeRow/removeColumn I'm considering the tricky case of removeColumn with an unknown key -- I'm unsure whether the underlying removeValue call would throw an UnknownKeyException since I can't see that implementation, so I'll stick to testing with known keys and note that removeColumn(int) could throw an index-out-of-bounds error from the underlying list access.

Now I'm sketching out clear(), equals() covering null, self-reference, wrong type, mismatched row/column keys, mismatched values, and null-vs-non-null value comparisons, plus hashCode() consistency checks and a clone() test verifying that mutating the original after cloning doesn't affect the copy. I'm also thinking about whether the test class needs to live in the same package to access DefaultKeyedValues and UnknownKeyException, or whether public methods alone suffice.

Writing test imports and setup...

Now I'm planning branch coverage for setValue, starting with the case of adding a new row.

I need to cover both sortRowKeys=true and false variants when adding new rows or columns, plus existing-key branches that skip the add, and also test getRowIndex with both sort settings and null arguments. For testing binary search insertion with sortRowKeys=true, I'll use String keys added out of order relying on natural alphabetical comparison.

Now I'm designing removeValue test cases: a 2x2 matrix where removing one value leaves the row non-null so it stays, a single-cell matrix where removal empties both the row and column so both get removed, and a shared-column scenario where one row becomes all-null and gets removed while the column survives because another row still has data there.

So column C2 gets removed since no remaining row has a value there, confirming the row-check-then-column-check ordering in the code. Since R1 was already removed before the column check runs, only R2 is considered, and it has no C2 entry, making the removal consistent. Now I'm tracing what happens when removing R2,C1 next.

When R2's only remaining value at C1 is removed, row R2 becomes empty and gets dropped too, and then the column check for C1 finds no rows left, so C1 is also removed—leaving the structure completely empty, which is a good cascade test case. I want to restructure this into clearer separate tests: one where both row and column survive, one where only the row becomes empty, and one where both become empty, and I'm sketching out the setup and assertions for the first case involving R1, R2, C1, and C2.

I'm laying out Test B where removing the last value from R1 empties that row while C1 survives because R2 still holds a value there, and Test C where removing the single value in the whole structure empties both the row and the column—covering all branches including the break-vs-no-break paths in the removal loops. Now I want to think about what comes next.

For getValue(int row, int column), I'm testing the index<0 branch by constructing rows where a row lacks a particular column key, so looking up a row/column combination that doesn't exist returns null via the -1 index path, while a normal lookup with a valid index exercises the other branch.

I also plan boundary tests for empty structures and out-of-bound exceptions on get calls, then comprehensive equals() tests covering null, self-equality, wrong type, differing row/column keys, differing values (null vs non-null), and full equality, followed by hashCode tests.

For hashCode, I'll verify equal objects share the same hash and confirm calling it on an empty structure doesn't throw. For clone(), I'll test that setting a value, cloning, then modifying the original doesn't affect the clone -- checking that adding a new row after cloning leaves the clone's row count unchanged, while noting rowKeys/columnKeys are shallow-copied since Strings are immutable.

Then I want to confirm the clone is truly deep by adding a value to an original row after cloning and checking the clone's value stays unaffected. For removeRow/removeColumn, I'll test removing by valid index updates the keys and data correctly, and test that removeRow with an unknown key currently throws IndexOutOfBoundsException due to getRowIndex returning -1 -- this is real observed behavior, not speculation, so it's worth capturing as a fault-detection test.

Since this is the Chart-18b Defects4J version, I should be careful not to assume the removeColumn(Comparable) fix is present -- I'll focus tests on known key removal rather than guessing unfixed-bug behavior. I also want a test confirming the default constructor sets sortRowKeys to false.

I'm planning to test insertion order for the default (unsorted) constructor versus sorted behavior when sortRowKeys is true -- inserting "B","A","C" should yield rowKeys sorted to ["A","B","C"], with getRowIndex using binary search returning correct positive indices.

I'll structure the final test class with setup helpers inline per test rather than a shared @Before, since several tests need distinct configurations. I'm listing out the test methods to write: default constructor state, normal value retrieval by index, null return when column missing from a row, updating an existing cell's value, insertion order under sorted row keys, and getRowIndex behavior with a null key.

Continuing to enumerate the remaining test cases I need to cover -- row/column index lookups under sorted and unsorted modes, null-key exceptions for both row and column index/value lookups, unmodifiable key collections, unknown-key exceptions, value removal scenarios (row-only, column-only, and both removed), row/column removal by index and key, clear behavior, and a full set of equals() tests comparing against null, same instance, different types, and differing row keys.

I still need equals tests for differing column keys and values, plus an equals test for matching structures, a hashCode consistency test, a clone test verifying deep copy of rows but shallow copy of keys, and boundary tests for getRowKey/getColumnKey with out-of-bounds indices. For exception assertions I'll mix `@Test(expected=...)` for simple cases with try/catch blocks when I need to verify state after the exception is thrown. Now I'm ready to write out the full test class.
